subject: Insurance
title: Fault vs. No-Fault States
description: A short lesson to help you apply Fault vs. No-Fault States.

hook.text: In a fault state, the at-fault driver's insurance pays everything.

buildup.text: 12 states plus Washington DC use no-fault systems.

discovery.text: In no-fault states, you can't sue the other driver unless injuries exceed a threshold.

twist.text: No-fault was meant to lower costs by reducing litigation.

climax.text: The fault system assigns blame and cost. No-fault distributes cost equally.

punchline.text: Fault: blame pays. No-fault: each pays their own.

quiz.question: How does a no-fault auto insurance system work?
options: Each driver's own insurance pays their medical bills regardless of fault
